questions.question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the italicised group of words.

The doctor prescribed a medicine that induces sleep to help the patient overcome his insomnia.
questions.solution: 'Soporific' is the appropriate one-word substitute for the underlined group of words. A 'soporific' is a substance that induces sleep or has a sleep-inducing effect. 'Veteran' refers to a person who has a lot of experience in a particular field, especially military service. 'Verbose' means containing more words than necessary. 'Hutch' refers to a cage for small animals, like rabbits or guinea pigs. Hence, (a) is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the bracketed group of words.

He was offered (a job with a high salary but little responsibility), which seemed appealing at first but left him feeling unfulfilled in the long run.
questions.solution: The appropriate one-word substitute for the underlined group of words is 'sinecure'. A 'sinecure' refers to a position or job that provides a salary or other benefits but requires little or no work. 'Hive' refers to a place where bees live and store honey. 'Plebiscite' is a direct vote by which the people of a region or country express their opinion on an important public question. 'Mint' refers to a place where coins are produced. Hence, (c) is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined group of words.

She sat by the window, lost in a feeling of deep sadness or sorrow.
questions.solution:
'Melancholy' means a feeling of deep sadness or sorrow. Hence, (b) is the correct answer.

'Jubilant' means feeling or expressing great joy or triumph.

'Enigma' means something that is mysterious, puzzling, or difficult to understand.

'Quintessential' means the most typical or perfect example of something.

questions.question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitution for the underlined group of words.

No one wanted him to drive as he drives like someone who behaves in a dangerous way.
questions.solution:
'Lunatic' means 'a person whose actions and manner are marked by extreme eccentricity or recklessness '.

Hence, option (d) is the answer.

'Insolvent' means 'unable to pay debts owed'.

'Narcissist' means 'a person who has an excessive interest in or admiration of themselves'.

'Polyglot' means 'knowing or using several languages'.

questions.question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined group of words.

The final result has shown that the worker has done the job without skill.
questions.solution:
Clumsy- done awkwardly or without skill.

Immature- not fully developed.

Flamboyant- to attract attention because of their exuberance, confidence, and stylishness.

Juvenile- for or relating to young people.

Among the given options, the word that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined phrase is option (a), 'clumsy'.

Hence, the correct answer is option (a).

questions.question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

A person who sacrifices his life for a cause
questions.solution: 'MARTYR' means 'A person who sacrifices his life for a cause.'. 'ACROPHOBIA' means 'Extreme or irrational fear of heights.'. 'ARBITRATOR' means 'An independent person or body officially appointed to settle a dispute.'. 'CONTEMPORARY' means 'A person or thing living or existing at the same time as another.'. According to the meanings mentioned above, option c) is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

A long, narrow box, typically of wood, in which a dead body is buried or cremated.
questions.solution:
Tombstone- A large, flat inscribed stone standing or laid over a grave.

Coffin- A long, narrow box, typically of wood, in which a dead body is buried or cremated.

Cemetery- A large burial ground, especially one not in a churchyard.

Burrow- A hole or tunnel dug by a small animal, especially a rabbit, as a dwelling.

The option that matches the meaning of the given group of words is (b), 'coffin'.

Hence, the correct answer is option (b).

questions.question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of italicised words.

Sarah's holding of her office ends by next year.
questions.solution:
Role- the function assumed or part played by a person or thing in a particular situation.

Position- a place where someone or something is located or has been put.

Rule- control of or dominion over an area or people.

Tenure- the holding of an office; the period of time when someone holds a job, esp. an official position, or the right to keep a job permanently.

Among the given options, the word that matches the meaning of the italicised words in the sentence is option (d), 'tenure'.

Hence, the correct answer is option (d).

questions.question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of italicised words.

The situation our country is facing now is extremely serious.
questions.solution:
Empathetic- showing an ability to understand and share the feelings of another.

Dire- extremely serious or urgent.

Stressful- causing mental or emotional stress.

Accommodative- willing to fit in with someone's wishes or needs

Among the given options, the word that matches the meaning of the italicised words in the sentence is option (b), 'dire'.

Hence, the correct answer is option (b).

questions.question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

To leave hurriedly and secretly
questions.solution: 'Abdicate' means to renounce one's throne. 'Ameliorate' means to make better. 'Aggravate' means to make worse. 'Abscond' means to run away. Hence, option (d) is the right answer.

questions.question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

An exact imitation or copy of written text
questions.solution:
Itinerary - a planned route or journey. Epicure - a person who takes pleasure in fine food or drink. Platitude - a remark that has been used too often to be meaningful. Facsimile - an exact copy of a written document.

Hence, option (d) is the answer.

questions.question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

Taking credit for someone else's writings or ideas
questions.solution:
'Covertness' is the quality of being hidden or unknown.

'Balk' means to hesitate or be unwilling to accept an idea or undertaking.

'Nuance' is a subtle, fine shade of meaning.

'Plagiarism' is the correct choice here, as it refers to taking credit for someone else's ideas.

Hence, option (b) is the right answer.

questions.question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

The practice of writing dictionaries
questions.solution:
WORDMEANING
GerontologyStudy of various aspects of ageing
NumismaticsStudy of collection of coins, tokens, paper money etc.
LexicographyThe practice of writing dictionaries
PhilologyThe study of languages

So, 'lexicography' is the right word.

Hence, option (c) is correct.

questions.question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

An organized course of action to achieve a goal.
questions.solution:
Effort- A vigorous or determined attempt.

Focus- The centre of interest or activity.

Campaign- An organized course of action to achieve a goal.

Direction- A course along which someone or something moves.

The option that matches the meaning of the given group of words is (c), 'campaign'.

Hence, the correct answer is option (c).

questions.question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

In a very difficult situation.
questions.solution:
Dangerous- Able or likely to cause harm or injury.

Beleaguered- In a very difficult situation.

Diligent- Having or showing care and conscientiousness in one's work or duties.

Bewildered- Perplexed and confused; very puzzled.

The option that matches the meaning of the given group of words is (b), 'beleaguered'.

Hence, the correct answer is option (b).

questions.question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

An automatic machine or container which is designed to release a specific amount of something.
questions.solution:
Dispenser- An automatic machine or container which is designed to release a specific amount of something.

Counter- A long, flat, narrow surface or table in a shop, bank, restaurant, etc. at which people are served.

Store- A shop of any size or kind.

Grocery- Items of food sold in a grocery or supermarket.

Among the given options, the word that matches the meaning of the given phrase is option (a), 'dispenser'.

Hence, the correct answer is option (a).

questions.question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the bracketed group of words.

He is a (person who talks too much).
questions.solution:
Let's look at the meanings of the given words.

Taciturn: (of a person) reserved or uncommunicative in speech; saying little.

Garrulous: excessively talkative, especially on trivial matters.

Generous: showing a readiness to give more of something, especially money, than is strictly necessary or expected.

Laconic: (of a person, speech, or style of writing) using very few words.

Among the given options, 'garrulous' is the correct choice.

Hence, option (b) is the correct answer.

questions.question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the given group of words.

Willing to give in to the wishes of another.
questions.solution:
'Amenable' means willing to give in to the wishes of another. Hence, (b) is the correct answer.

'Amiable' means having or displaying a friendly and pleasant manner.

'Amorphous' means without a clearly defined shape or form.

'Analogy' means a comparison between two things, typically for the purpose of explanation or clarification.

questions.question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the italicised group of words.

She thinks that she has the quality of being religious and is qualified enough to preach it to others.
questions.solution:
Piety- the quality of being religious or reverent.

Priesthood- the office or position of a priest.

Morality- principles concerning the distinction between right and wrong or good and bad behaviour.

Abhorrence- a feeling of revulsion; disgusted loathing.

Among the given options, the word that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined phrase is option (a), 'piety'.

Hence, the correct answer is option (a).

questions.question:
Select the option that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined group of words.

After the war, all the prisoners will be kept in the strong underground prison cell, in the castle.
questions.solution:
Graveyard- a burial ground, especially one beside a church.

Prison- a building in which people are legally held as a punishment for a crime they have committed or while awaiting trial.

Dungeon- a strong underground prison cell, especially in a castle.

Cubicle- a small partitioned-off area of a room, for example, one containing a shower or toilet, or a desk in an office.

Among the given options, the word that can be used as a one-word substitute for the underlined phrase is option (c), 'dungeon'.

Hence, the correct answer is option (c).
